public.title: Bound Function Calls
public.description: Model binding a numeric receiver and leading arguments. A function returns base minus the sum of all arguments. Bind the receiver base and the prefix bound, then invoke for every argument-array in calls. Return the numeric results. This adapter exercises partial application and receiver capture, not constructors. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Captured arguments precede arguments from each later call.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Keep the bound receiver and prefix independent of each call. Concatenate prefix and call arguments and subtract their sum from base. O(total supplied arguments plus bound length times call count) time; O(bound length plus largest call length) auxiliary space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
